key_insight: Increasing cylinder rotation suppresses conventional vortex shedding before unsteadiness re-emerges at higher rotation with intermittent, multiscale dynamics.
engineering_relevance: Rotation offers a way to reshape wake dynamics and aerodynamic loading, but high rotation can introduce renewed fluctuations and appreciable local compressibility.
method: 130 high-fidelity simulations of two-dimensional compressible flow at Re∞ = 3800 and M∞ = 0.1.
Rotation-rate sweep over 0.1 ≤ Ω ≤ 10 with surface-pressure and skin-friction analysis.
Vorticity-based proper orthogonal decomposition to characterize coherent flow structures.
evidence_signal: The simulations identify a narrow transition around Ω = 2.2–2.8 toward nearly quiescent flow, while higher rotation produces renewed unsteadiness and local Mach numbers approaching 0.5.
watch_item: The findings are limited to two-dimensional simulations at one free-stream Reynolds and Mach number; applicability to three-dimensional engineering flows requires validation.
paper_title: Rotation-driven suppression and re-emergence of unsteady flow past a circular cylinder
